title: DB-HDFFN: Dual Branch Hierarchical Dynamic Feature Fusion Network for medical image classification

proposed_method_detail.method_name: DB-HDFFN (Dual Branch Hierarchical Dynamic Feature Fusion Network)

model_family.name: Transformer
model_family.role: Global Feature Learner (Dynamic Sparse Attention Block)

model_family.name: CNN
model_family.role: Local Feature Learner (Intra-Inter Variance Feature Extracting Block)

contributions.improvement: Noise-robust and computation-efficient global modeling by addressing irrelevant information.
contributions.implementation_detail: Developed a Dynamic Sparse Attention Block (DSA-Block) with a novel top-k dynamic sparsification strategy that selectively preserves the most informative regions.
contributions.improve_from: Existing Transformer-based methods that apply full attention and are easily distracted by irrelevant regions.

contributions.improvement: Accurately capturing fine-grained pathological patterns in complex lesion areas by adaptively emphasizing subtle lesion regions and suppressing misleading anatomical variations.
contributions.implementation_detail: Designed an Intra-Inter Variance Feature Extracting Block (ICV-Block) that leverages the inherent property of significant intra-image variance and relatively slight inter-image variance in medical images.
contributions.improve_from: Existing vision models that largely overlooked the unique variance property of medical images.

contributions.improvement: Effective integration of multi-scale global and local representations.
contributions.implementation_detail: Proposed a Dynamic Fusion Block (DF-Block) that performs hierarchical cross-branch fusion via channel attention and dynamic convolution, effectively preserving complementary characteristics.

contributions.improvement: Overall superior performance in medical image classification across multiple datasets.
contributions.implementation_detail: The proposed Dual-Branch Hierarchical Dynamic Feature Fusion Network (DB-HDFFN) combines the DSA-Block, ICV-Block, and DF-Block.
contributions.improve_from: Other state-of-the-art models (CNN-based, Transformer-based, and fusion-based methods).

limitations: Currently designed for 2D images; extending to 3D modalities may require redesigning attention and variance-aware modules for volumetric consistency.
Dynamic components introduce overhead, suggesting the need for lighter, more efficient variants.
Relies on fully supervised learning and may be less effective on datasets with limited annotations.
